messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Key Points (2024)** | Topic | Summary | Notes | |-------|---------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the maximum speed you may drive.
• On highways, limits range from 55 mph to 85 mph.
• In residential areas, limits are usually 25–35 mph. | • Exceeding posted limits can result in fines, points, and possible license suspension. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster.
• The law applies to all vehicles, including motorcycles (helmet required). | • Failure to comply can lead to a $50 fine and 1 point on the driver’s record. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | • Violations carry a $50 fine and 1 point. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• For commercial drivers, the limit is 0.04%.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | • First offense: up to 90 days in jail, $500 fine, 90‑day license suspension. | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red lights: stop; Yellow: prepare to stop; Green: go.
• Stop signs: come to a full stop before proceeding. | • Running a red light or stop sign can result in a $200 fine and 2 points. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has priority.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | • Disobeying right‑of‑way can lead to fines and points. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Use turn signals when changing lanes or turning. | • Failure to signal can result in a $50 fine and 1 point. | | **School Bus** | • Stop for a school bus with its stop sign extended and lights flashing.
• Vehicles traveling in either direction must stop. | • Violations can lead to a $200 fine and 2 points. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in no‑stop zones, fire lanes, or within 20 ft of a crosswalk.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is illegal. | • Parking violations can result in fines and towing. | | **Vehicle Equipment** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise.
• Tires must have adequate tread depth (minimum 2 / 32 in). | • Failure to comply can lead to a $50 fine and 1 point. | | **Points System** | • Accumulating 4 points in 2 years can lead to license suspension.
• Points are added for various infractions (speeding, DUI, etc.). | • Points can be reduced through defensive‑driving courses. | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury, $25,000 for property damage. | • Driving without insurance can result in license suspension and fines. | ### How to Stay Updated - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)**: Official source for statutes, regulations, and updates. - **Texas Transportation Code**: The legal text governing all traffic laws. - **Local County Courts**: For specific local ordinances that may differ (e.g., speed limits in city limits). ### Quick Tips 1. **Always obey posted signs and signals.** 2. **Use hands‑free devices if you need to use your phone.** 3. **Keep your vehicle’s equipment (headlights, tires, brakes) in good condition.** 4. **Carry proof of insurance and registration.** 5. **If you’re unsure about a law, check the Texas DPS website or consult a local attorney.** Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to handle a particular traffic violation!
